questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The academic tradition; the importance of continental philosophy in Leuven

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Quite easy

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I don't think I received anything, but I did not miss it either.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was difficult. I strongly under estimated how difficult it was to find housing in Leuven. I thought it was a lot easier than it is in Copenhagen, but it turned out to be a real struggle.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Try to find something on campus. It is cheaper, and more reliable. Begin to search for housing months before.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You register whatever course you wish to take on uni-website. Very easy. And I found it very nice that I could choose whatever I wanted. There are no limits on the amount of students on the courses, so there is no stress about that. One can do whatever one wants, which is very nice.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The institute is very open for helping. I mailed them when in struggle and they replied very quickly.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Extremely successful - I got in to all the courses I wanted, and everyone else does as well (as far as I know)

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: No advice from me. Look up all courses one could be interested in and try to read the descriptions carefully.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Very high levels (on philosophy courses). The institute has a long and proud tradition for its philosophy and it is very ambitious. I am not used to the high expectations and high ambitions and this was both very inspiring and stressful.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching itself is similar, I think.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Contiental philosophy, Phenomenology and Contemporary Continental Philosophy, Phenomenology (Texts): Seminar

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Housing first of all. I paid way more than what the usual student does.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I thought that food was cheaper, but it is very similar to Danish prices.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Sports centre, I did not use it. ESN (Erasmus student network) (arrange both sports, cultural and social events).

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Try to connect with people from your institute (Institute of Philosophy). People there helped me a lot and guided me through the local and cultural life, and gave me lots of recommendation. I also joined the introduction week, but did not really enjoy it. However, I got friends which I hung out with the first months. It was helpfull, but I ended spending more time with philosophy students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I did not travel around a lot, but simply just drank beers and danced during the weekends. I enjoyed this as it felt more like home, as I did not go out travelling every weekend in CPH. Try to hang out with people both in clubs/bars but also in friends' homes.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just be yourself.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The study culture - very disciplined and stresfull. As the university expects more from the students than they do in CPH (for example way more learning by heart), one simply needs to study a lot. I find this a bit toxic. Too much pressure, though also inspiring at moments.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The culture of the institute, contiental philosophy.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Take care of yourself in the exam period. It is going to be extremely tough (6 exams) 
Be open to people that does not look like yourself. 
Be disciplined and choose courses you really like.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Continental philosophy (it is a thing in Leuven!). In CPH, it has becomes so penetrated by analytic philopshy that many professors simply ignore that there are others way of thinking. In Leuven, the understanding of what philosophy is way broader and more openminded that it is in CPH.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: 6 exams (+ essays, presentation). Very stressful, full of panic attacks.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
